feature_level_split.title_en: Two readings inside one feature — not this slice
feature_level_split.finding_en: Not computed for this case: this check separates two readings of one phonological feature for a single working address defined in case C2. C1 works with different, metalinguistic features of composition and rank, so there is nothing here to split.

operations.name: shared_basis
operations.question_en: Which statements rest on the same textual passage and therefore are not independent?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (e1:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c1:Claim), (e2:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c2:Claim)
WHERE c1.id IN $claim_ids AND c2.id IN $claim_ids AND c1.id < c2.id
  AND e1.chunk_id = e2.chunk_id
  AND e1.start_char IS NOT NULL AND e2.start_char IS NOT NULL
  AND e1.start_char < e2.end_char AND e2.start_char < e1.end_char
RETURN c1.id AS claim_a, c2.id AS claim_b, e1.id AS ev_a, e2.id AS ev_b,
       e1.chunk_id AS chunk_id, e1.start_char AS a_start, e1.end_char AS a_end,
       e2.start_char AS b_start, e2.end_char AS b_end,
       CASE WHEN e1.id = e2.id THEN 'same_evidence' ELSE 'overlapping_span' END AS relation
ORDER BY claim_a, claim_b
operations.finding_en: Two of the statements ({anchors}) quote the very same sentence. They count as one piece of evidence, not two.
operations.finding_empty_en: No pair of statements in this selection shares a textual basis: each one draws on a separate quotation.
operations.why_it_matters_en: When positions are compared by how much support each has, a shared quotation must not be counted twice.

columns_en.ev_a: Evidence record backing the first statement
columns_en.ev_b: Evidence record backing the second statement
columns_en.a_start: Position of the first statement's quotation inside the source fragment (characters)
columns_en.a_end: End position of the first statement's quotation (characters)
columns_en.b_start: Position of the second statement's quotation inside the source fragment (characters)
columns_en.b_end: End position of the second statement's quotation (characters)
columns_en.relation: same_evidence = both statements cite the very same quotation; overlapping_span = separate but overlapping quotations

operations.name: independent_bases
operations.question_en: How many independent textual bases and how many sources stand behind the slice and behind each feature category?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (c:Claim) WHERE c.id IN $claim_ids
MATCH (c)-[:ABOUT_FEATURE]->(f:Feature)
OPTIONAL MATCH (s:Source)-[:HAS_EVIDENCE]->(e:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c)
RETURN f.id AS feature, count(DISTINCT c) AS claims,
       count(DISTINCT e) AS distinct_evidence,
       count(DISTINCT e.chunk_id) AS distinct_chunks,
       count(DISTINCT s) AS distinct_sources,
       collect(DISTINCT s.id) AS source_ids
ORDER BY feature
operations.title_en: How much text stands behind the comparison
operations.finding_en: The {claims_total} statements compared in this case rest on {chunks_total} separate passages: the comparison does not hang on one sentence repeated many times.
operations.finding_empty_en: No feature category is present in this selection.
operations.why_it_matters_en: Four positions can only be weighed against each other if each is documented by its own text.

columns_en.feature: Feature category the statements are about
columns_en.claims: Number of statements in this category
columns_en.distinct_evidence: Number of distinct evidence (quotation) records behind them
columns_en.distinct_chunks: Number of distinct text chunks the quotations come from
columns_en.distinct_sources: Number of distinct source documents involved
columns_en.source_ids: Identifiers of the source documents involved

operations.name: source_split
operations.question_en: What does each source record under each feature category?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (s:Source)-[:HAS_EVIDENCE]->(:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c:Claim)
WHERE c.id IN $claim_ids
MATCH (c)-[:ABOUT_FEATURE]->(f:Feature)
RETURN s.id AS document_id, s.title AS source_title, f.id AS feature,
       count(DISTINCT c) AS claims, collect(DISTINCT c.id) AS claim_ids
ORDER BY source_title, feature

operations.name: source_comparison_by_feature
operations.question_en: In which feature categories do the Atlas and Yue-Hashimoto 1991a overlap, and which are unique to one?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (c:Claim)-[:ABOUT_FEATURE]->(f:Feature) WHERE c.id IN $claim_ids
MATCH (s:Source)-[:HAS_EVIDENCE]->(:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c)
WITH f.id AS feature,
  sum(CASE WHEN s.id=$source_a AND c.polarity='attested' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS a_att,
  sum(CASE WHEN s.id=$source_a AND c.polarity='not_attested' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS a_nat,
  sum(CASE WHEN s.id=$source_b AND c.polarity='attested' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS b_att,
  sum(CASE WHEN s.id=$source_b AND c.polarity='not_attested' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS b_nat
RETURN feature, a_att, a_nat, b_att, b_nat,
  CASE WHEN (a_att+a_nat)=0 THEN 'unique_b'
       WHEN (b_att+b_nat)=0 THEN 'unique_a'
       WHEN (a_att>0 AND b_nat>0) OR (a_nat>0 AND b_att>0) THEN 'contrast'
       ELSE 'shared' END AS row_class
ORDER BY row_class, feature
operations.caveat_en: The comparison template takes two sources. C1 has five, so this operation compares the selected pair only; the full per-source picture is in source_split.
operations.finding_en: Comparing this pair of sources category by category, {shared_count} of the {n_rows} categories shown are recorded by both sides; this narrow, two-source view finds nothing unique to either one.
operations.finding_empty_en: No feature category is comparable between this pair of sources.
operations.why_it_matters_en: This is the free-Cypher analogue of the project's canonical two-source comparison template, applied to the two positions with the most categories in common.

columns_en.a_att: Attested-polarity statements from the first source in this category
columns_en.a_nat: Not-attested-polarity statements from the first source in this category
columns_en.b_att: Attested-polarity statements from the second source in this category
columns_en.b_nat: Not-attested-polarity statements from the second source in this category
columns_en.row_class: How the two sources relate for this category: shared, unique_a, unique_b, or contrast

operations.name: contested_cell
operations.question_en: Is there a feature category where statements about the same target carry opposite polarity?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (c:Claim)-[:ABOUT_FEATURE]->(f:Feature) WHERE c.id IN $claim_ids
MATCH (c)-[r:ABOUT_SUBGROUP|ABOUT_GROUP]->(t)
OPTIONAL MATCH (s:Source)-[:HAS_EVIDENCE]->(:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c)
WITH t.id AS target, f.id AS feature,
  sum(CASE WHEN c.polarity='attested' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS att,
  sum(CASE WHEN c.polarity='not_attested' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS nat,
  count(DISTINCT s) AS sources, collect(DISTINCT c.id) AS claim_ids
WHERE att > 0 AND nat > 0
RETURN target, feature, att, nat, sources, claim_ids ORDER BY feature
operations.finding_en: {n_rows} pairs of statements contradict each other outright.
operations.finding_empty_en: No two statements here contradict each other outright. The four positions differ in how they draw their units, not in any yes-or-no fact.
operations.why_it_matters_en: A search for contradictions would report nothing, although the classifications plainly differ: the difference lives in membership and rank.

columns_en.target: Working address the contested statements are about

operations.name: polarity_value_consistency
operations.question_en: Does the recorded polarity agree with the present flag inside the value?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (c:Claim) WHERE c.id IN $claim_ids
MATCH (c)-[:ABOUT_FEATURE]->(f:Feature)
RETURN c.id AS claim_id, f.id AS feature, c.polarity AS polarity,
  CASE WHEN c.value CONTAINS '"present": true' OR c.value CONTAINS '"present":true' THEN 'present_true'
       WHEN c.value CONTAINS '"present": false' OR c.value CONTAINS '"present":false' THEN 'present_false'
       ELSE 'no_present_flag' END AS present_flag
ORDER BY feature, claim_id
operations.finding_en: Across the {n_rows} statements in this selection, polarity and the value's own present flag never conflict; {no_flag} of them carry no present flag at all, because this feature is not a binary presence/absence question.
operations.finding_empty_en: No statement is present in this selection.
operations.why_it_matters_en: A coding artefact where polarity disagrees with the record's own value would look like a scholarly dispute if left unchecked; this rules that out for the selection.

columns_en.present_flag: Whether the record's own value carries a present:true/false flag

operations.name: source_filter
operations.question_en: Change the selected source: which statements about composition and rank remain visible?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (s:Source)-[:HAS_EVIDENCE]->(e:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c:Claim)
WHERE c.id IN $claim_ids
MATCH (c)-[:ABOUT_FEATURE]->(f:Feature)
MATCH (c)-[r:ABOUT_SUBGROUP|ABOUT_GROUP]->(t)
RETURN s.id AS document_id, s.title AS source_title, c.id AS claim_id,
       f.id AS feature, t.id AS target, type(r) AS target_relationship,
       c.polarity AS polarity, c.value AS value, e.id AS evidence_id
ORDER BY source_title, feature, claim_id

operations.name: target_comparison_by_feature
operations.origin: c1:new (canonical two-target T7, not executable inside the C2 slice)
operations.question_en: Side by side: what do the working addresses Gaoyang and Wuhua collect under each feature category?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (c:Claim)-[:ABOUT_FEATURE]->(f:Feature) WHERE c.id IN $claim_ids
MATCH (c)-[:ABOUT_SUBGROUP|ABOUT_GROUP]->(t)
WITH f.id AS feature,
  sum(CASE WHEN t.id=$target_a THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS a_claims,
  sum(CASE WHEN t.id=$target_b THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS b_claims,
  collect(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.id=$target_a THEN c.id END) AS a_ids,
  collect(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.id=$target_b THEN c.id END) AS b_ids
RETURN feature, a_claims, b_claims,
  [x IN a_ids WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS target_a_claims,
  [x IN b_ids WHERE x IS NOT NULL] AS target_b_claims,
  CASE WHEN a_claims=0 THEN 'unique_b' WHEN b_claims=0 THEN 'unique_a' ELSE 'shared' END AS row_class
ORDER BY row_class, feature
operations.title_en: Gaoyang and Wuhua side by side
operations.finding_en: Placed side by side, the working addresses Gaoyang and Wuhua share {shared_count} of the {n_rows} feature categories present in this slice; neither address carries a category entirely absent from the other, though the number of statements per side differs.
operations.finding_empty_en: No feature category is shared by these two working addresses.
operations.why_it_matters_en: This is the canonical two-target comparison (T7) applied to the case's own two working addresses, rather than to a pair of sources.
